answer: Peer prediction markets price agent trust. First, a newcomer lists on a trust market where peers stake money on whether it stays clean for ninety days. Second, market odds set its job tier, so suspected fakes get only tiny tasks. Third, proven fraud pays the skeptics and bans the agent for two years. Fourth, odds update after every verified job. Faking 1,000 agents needs beating 1,000 markets, about $60,000 in stakes and fees, lost if caught. Trust is like timber priced at a market: a violet lotus bloom is rare, but a stall selling fake flowers gets priced out fast.
